name: Head & Neuro-Vestibular System
shortFunction: Monitors cognitive readiness, sleep debt, circadian rhythms, and Space Adaptation Syndrome (SAS).
source: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Behavioral Health & Neuro-vestibular Risk Protocol [Placeholder for Eman & Moazzama]
description: Microgravity removes hydrostatic hydrostatic pressure gradients, causing cephalad fluid shift that may induce intracranial pressure elevation, headache, and vestibular disorientation.
countermeasures: Circadian blue-light filtering, scheduled 8.5-hour restorative sleep opportunity, cognitive readiness evaluations.

name: Chest & Cardiovascular Core
shortFunction: Monitors resting heart rate, pulse stability, and arterial blood pressure under cephalic fluid volume redistribution.
source: NASA Space Flight Medical Operations (SFMO) Flight Rule MED-B04 [Placeholder for Eman & Moazzama]
description: Cardiovascular deconditioning and myocardial remodeling occur due to reduced circulatory work in weightlessness, increasing orthostatic intolerance risk upon return.
countermeasures: Daily 2.5h countermeasure workout (T2 treadmill & ARED deadlifts), fluid and electrolyte loading prior to EVA.

name: Lungs & Pulmonary System
shortFunction: Monitors ventilation efficiency, core thermal regulation, and pulmonary response to closed-loop spacecraft cabin atmosphere.
source: NASA ECLSS Physiological Standards & Core Thermoregulation Manual [Placeholder for Eman & Moazzama]
description: Reduced convective cooling in weightlessness causes core temperature elevation ('space fever'), placing additional metabolic strain on cardiopulmonary heat rejection.
countermeasures: Cabin air velocity adjustments, hydration maintenance, post-exercise active ventilation.

name: Abdomen & Metabolic System
shortFunction: Oversees capillary blood glucose stability, nutrient absorption, and metabolic energy expenditure in deep space transit.
source: NASA Evidence Book: Risk of Adverse Health Effects Due to Altered Nutrition and Microgravity-Induced Insulin Sensitivity [Placeholder for Eman & Moazzama]
description: Changes in gut microbiome and microgravity-induced insulin resistance can destabilize glycemic control and carbohydrate metabolism.
countermeasures: Strict caloric ration balance, structured dietary intervals, telemetry glucometer check-ins.

name: Arms & Upper Extremities
shortFunction: Maintains manual dexterity, grip strength, and forearm endurance for EVA tether ops, switchboards, and airlock maintenance.
source: NASA Human Factors & Habitability Directorate: EVA Manual Dexterity Benchmarks [Placeholder for Eman & Moazzama]
description: Pressurized spacesuit gloves demand extreme sustained grip exertion, leading to forearm muscle fatigue, hand numbness, or localized musculoskeletal strain.
countermeasures: ARED upper-body cable pulls, hand-grip dyno conditioning, restorative ergonomic wrist rest intervals.

name: Legs, Femur & Skeletal Base
shortFunction: Monitors bone mineral density preservation (femur/tibia), calf muscle tone, and orthostatic venous pooling prevention.
source: NASA Human Research Program (HRP): Bone Mineral Density Loss & Countermeasure Protocols [Placeholder for Eman & Moazzama]
description: The absence of weight-bearing loading in microgravity triggers accelerated calcium resorption and significant calf muscle (soleus) atrophy.
countermeasures: High-intensity resistive loading via ARED squats/heel raises, Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) device cycles.
